summary:
SOLIS (Solar Observations and Landing Interface System) is an interactive lunar mission planning platform designed to simplify the evaluation and planning of missions to the Moon, particularly its south pole. The platform brings scientific data analysis, mission simulations, and robotic operations together in a unified environment.

SOLIS enables users to explore potential landing sites by analyzing terrain elevation, slope, solar illumination, Earth visibility, temperature, and potential water ice resources. It also supports launch and return planning through orbital analysis, trajectory simulations, and AI-assisted evaluation of possible mission dates and routes.

For lunar surface operations, SOLIS provides rover route planning and integrates with a physical NASA JPL Open Source Rover through ROS 2, enabling command exchange and telemetry monitoring.

By connecting landing site assessment, mission planning, simulation, and real-world robotics, SOLIS aims to make complex lunar mission scenarios easier to explore, visualize, and evaluate.
details:
SOLIS — Project Details

1. Project Overview

SOLIS (Solar Observations and Landing Interface System) is an interactive platform that connects the major stages of lunar mission planning, from landing site selection and launch planning to surface exploration and Earth return. Its primary focus is the challenges of lunar south pole missions, where extreme lighting conditions, difficult terrain, and limited communication opportunities make mission planning particularly complex.

Instead of treating these challenges as separate problems, SOLIS brings them together in a unified environment where users can analyze, visualize, and evaluate an entire lunar mission.

2. Scientific Analysis & Landing Site Selection

SOLIS allows users to explore and compare potential lunar landing sites using scientific and environmental information. Its analysis considers several important factors:

  • Terrain Analysis: Elevation, slope, surface characteristics, and potential hazards.
  • Solar Conditions: Sun position, elevation, and illumination periods.
  • Earth Visibility: Visibility conditions and potential communication windows.
  • Environmental Analysis: Surface temperature, thermal variations, and shadow conditions.
  • Water Ice Potential: Indicators of potentially valuable lunar resources.
  • Landing Safety: Terrain conditions and potential touchdown risks.
  • Scientific Value: Exploration opportunities and areas of scientific interest.

These factors contribute to a multi-criteria evaluation system that helps users compare candidate landing locations and understand the advantages and limitations of each site.

3. Mission Planning & AI-Assisted Analysis

SOLIS extends beyond landing site selection by supporting mission planning and trajectory visualization. Users can configure mission parameters, evaluate potential launch opportunities, and explore simulated Earth-to-Moon trajectories.

Machine learning models, including regression-based approaches and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), are incorporated into the platform for predictive analysis and the evaluation of mission scenarios.

For the return phase, AI-assisted analysis helps evaluate potential departure dates and alternative return scenarios. These results can be compared through estimated travel durations and visualized trajectories, supporting more informed mission planning.

4. Lunar Surface Operations & Robotics Integration

One of SOLIS's distinctive features is its connection to a physical robotic platform. The system integrates with the NASA JPL Open Source Rover (OSR) through ROS 2.

Planned rover movements are translated into a custom ROS 2-compatible command format, allowing the platform to exchange commands with the physical rover. ROS 2 communication also enables telemetry reception, connecting mission planning with real-world robotic control and monitoring.

The platform additionally supports lunar surface route planning, considering terrain conditions, obstacles, and route efficiency.

5. Technologies & Development Tools

SOLIS was developed using a combination of web technologies, scientific computing tools, machine learning methods, and robotics software.

  • Frontend: React
  • 3D Visualization: Three.js
  • Programming & Scientific Computing: Python, NumPy, SciPy, Astropy
  • Machine Learning: Regression Analysis, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs)
  • Robotics: ROS 2, NASA JPL Open Source Rover
  • Orbital Analysis: NASA JPL Horizons, NASA SPICE
  • Lunar Data: NASA Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) datasets

6. Creativity, Benefits & Intended Impact

The main innovation behind SOLIS is the integration of scientific analysis, AI-assisted decision-making, interactive mission simulations, and physical robotics into a single workflow.

While many tools focus on individual aspects of lunar exploration, SOLIS aims to connect these stages and make their relationships easier to understand. Users can investigate how landing site conditions influence mission feasibility, explore different mission scenarios, plan robotic surface operations, and evaluate possible return strategies.

By making complex lunar mission concepts more accessible and interactive, SOLIS can support students, educators, space enthusiasts, and early-stage mission planning research. Ultimately, our goal is to provide a unified environment for exploring the challenges of lunar exploration and understanding what it takes to plan a mission from Earth to the Moon and back.
